public_rationale: Marcus said multiple studies show the major LLMs have not been very different from one another. Two comparative studies came out before his post on 21 June 2025. Rozado's peer-reviewed study in PLOS ONE (July 2024) gave 11 political tests to 24 conversational LLMs. Most of those LLMs gave answers that most of the tests rated left of center (e1). A Stanford study described in May 2025 gave 30 political questions to 24 LLMs from 8 companies. On 18 of the 30 questions, users saw nearly all responses as left-leaning (e2). The Stanford study also found differences in degree. OpenAI's perceived slant was four times Google's, and Google and DeepSeek were statistically indistinguishable from neutral on average (e3). The summary does not report any company's models as right-leaning. The contract asks for two or more studies placing most major LLMs in the same broad area. Both studies place most tested models between neutral and left of center, so the support condition is met. The reported gaps are differences in degree. They are not the clearly opposite positions that the contradiction condition requires.
limitations: 'Not that different' sets no threshold. A stricter reading could give more weight to the four-fold gap between companies.
The PLOS article itself could not be read. The official press release was used instead.
The Stanford evidence is a business-school summary of user perceptions, not the full paper. It does not give the position of every company's models.
Both studies measure political views only, not other kinds of differences between models.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: So far, the major LLMs have not differed much from one another in the views they express.

statement.excerpt: It turns out that, thus far, the major LLMs haven’t been that different from one another, as multiple studies have shown.

from_speaker: the major LLMs haven't been that different from one another
our_interpretation: In context, 'not that different' means the views major chatbots express, mainly political ones. The claim holds if published comparisons of several major models found them leaning the same way and sitting in a narrow range, even if they differ somewhat in degree.
'Thus far' covers the period from the launch of ChatGPT in late 2022 to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Two or more published comparative studies, out by mid-2025, find that most major LLMs land in the same broad area (for example, all mildly left of center) on political or opinion measures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Published comparative studies find that major LLMs take clearly different positions on these measures, for example some clearly left and others clearly right.

evidence.excerpt: He found that most of the tested conversational LLMs generated responses diagnosed by the majority of the political test instruments used here as left-of-center viewpoints.
evidence.explanation: In a peer-reviewed study of 24 major LLMs, most landed in the same left-of-center area. That is consistent with the models not being very different.

evidence.excerpt: For 18 of the 30 questions, users perceived nearly all of the LLMs’ responses as left-leaning.
evidence.explanation: A second study, of 24 LLMs from 8 companies, found that nearly all of them leaned the same way. This is a second study showing the models cluster.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI models had the most intensely perceived left-leaning slant — four times greater than perceptions of Google, whose models were perceived as the least slanted overall. On average, models from Google and DeepSeek were seen as statistically indistinguishable from neutral
evidence.explanation: The degree of slant varied, by up to four times between companies. But every company ranged from neutral to left, with none clearly right. This limits the claim but does not reverse it.
